summary: A map of the world, a continent, a country or a frame fitted to a list of places (Natural Earth, public domain): land or countries with borders, highlighted countries, countries coloured through a ramp with a legend, city markers with labels, a route or several labelled legs, a marker from host lon/lat, and an optional day/night shade from the clock. It scales to fit the box it gets, and opt-in for a world clock: a soft twilight edge on the night shade, the sun over the subsolar point and city markers that light up where the sun is up.

region.doc: "world" (no Antarctica), "world-full", a continent (Europe, Africa, Asia, North America, South America, Oceania), a subregion ("Western Europe"), a country (ISO "FRA"/"FR" or its name: its main landmass) or [lonMin, latMin, lonMax, latMax], or a list of places to frame tightly: countries, cities, [lon, lat] and [from, to] pairs (their great circle), e.g. ["Dubai", "London", "Singapore"]: padded for markers and labels and shaped like a card (1.25:1 to 2.4:1)

detail.doc: Outline detail: low for a widget (a world of land is ~6 KB), medium for a screen, high for a large country map. Each level roughly doubles the bytes

borders.doc: Draw countries with borders instead of plain land

highlight.doc: Countries to fill in highlightColor (ISO A3/A2 or names), e.g. ["FRA", "DE"]

cities.doc: City markers by name (Natural Earth's 1,250 places, every capital and state capital: "Tokyo", "New York"...)

labels.doc: Write each city's name beside its marker

markLon.doc: One marker the app moves: longitude (a "@variable"); give markLat too

night.doc: Shade the night side from the clock (world regions only): solar declination from the day of the year, the sun's longitude from UTC time. Repaints once a minute

values.doc: Countries coloured at run time: a float array "@name" (resources.floatArrays, export it for the app), one value per country of valueCountries in the same order: 0 leaves it as land, 1 fills it in valueColor, between blends (a choropleth: visited 0/1, a share 0..1)

valueCountries.doc: The countries of values, in the array's order (ISO A3/A2 or names), e.g. ["FRA", "DEU", "ESP"]. map_info lists a region's countries. A country too small to outline at the detail (Monaco, Malta) is a dot

valueColor.doc: The fill of a country whose value is 1 (mono: onSurface)

ramp.doc: Colour values through a ramp instead of a fade into valueColor: 2 or more colours, low to high, e.g. ["#FFE3F2FD", "#FF1565C0"] or ["@colors.success", "@colors.warning", "@colors.error"]. valueMin is the first, valueMax the last, evenly spaced between; a value below valueMin leaves its country as land (no data). In mono: four classes, hatched, cross-hatched, grey and solid

valueMin.doc: The value at the ramp's first colour (with ramp)

valueMax.doc: The value at the ramp's last colour (with ramp)

legend.doc: A scale bar for the ramp under the map, valueMin at its left end and valueMax with units at its right (mono: the four class swatches). The map shrinks to leave it room

legendDecimals.doc: Decimals of the legend's numbers (they are grouped: 1,500)

units.doc: Written after valueMax on the legend ("%", "€/MWh")

pointsLon.doc: Points from the app: a float array "@name" of longitudes (any count, the app can change it); give pointsLat too. Each is a dot of markerSize

pointsLat.doc: The latitudes of pointsLon, same order

routeFrom.doc: A great-circle route from this place (a city name, or "lon,lat" like "2.55,49.01") to routeTo, drawn in routeColor with a dot at each end

routeTo.doc: Where the route ends (a city name or "lon,lat")

progress.doc: How far along the route, 0..1 (a "@variable" the app or the clock drives): the flown part is drawn in flownColor and a plane icon sits at it, turned to its heading. Omit for a route only

plane.doc: Draw the plane icon at progress (false: a dot)

flownColor.doc: The part flown, the plane and the end dots

legs.doc: Several routes, each its own great-circle arc in legColor with a dot at each end: [{"from": "Dubai", "to": "London", "label": "EK 1"}, ...] or [from, to, label] (cities or "lon,lat"). Each label sits on its arc with a halo, placed so the labels miss each other, the leg ends and their city names

legDistance.doc: Label each leg that has no label with its great-circle distance ("5,473 km")

legColor.doc: The legs' arcs and end dots

states.doc: Draw state/province borders of these countries (ISO A3): AUS, USA, CAN, IND, BRA, CHN, RUS, ZAF, ARG, IDN, DEU, JPN, MEX, ESP, ITA, GBR, FRA ...

fit.doc: Places to frame, instead of region: countries, cities, [lon, lat] and [from, to] pairs, e.g. ["Dubai", "London", "Singapore"]. They fit the box both ways at the largest scale, centred, with the geography around them filling the rest (a box from 0.9:1 to 2.6:1 is filled). Text then scales with the map (0.8x to 1.8x labelSize); city names (cities with labels) and leg labels are placed together, and a label that would touch a more important one at a small size is hidden: cities in their order first, then legs

fill.doc: Take the height left in the parent column (a vertical weight) instead of height: the map grows and shrinks with the window. The region is drawn at the largest scale that fits, centred, with the geography around it filling the rest of the box (not for a world, or with night); text, dots and lines scale with the map (0.8x to 1.8x), and labels that would collide on a small screen are hidden

height.doc: Height in dp (the map keeps its aspect inside: a world is 2.5:1)

sea.doc: Sea fill behind the land (none by default: the surface shows)

nightColor.doc: Night shade colour (light and dark looks; black darkens both). In mono the shade is always the theme's onSurface at nightAlpha, whatever this is

twilight.doc: With night: a soft terminator, the shade drawn three times 5 degrees of longitude apart (deep night gets all three, the edges one or two; together they make nightAlpha). In mono the night edge is also drawn as a line

sun.doc: Draw the sun over the subsolar point (where it is overhead now), from the clock: a disc in sunColor with a soft glow (mono: a disc in a ring). World regions only

sunColor.doc: The sun's disc and glow (mono: onSurface)

daylight.doc: The city markers (cities) light up where the sun is up: dayColor with a halo by day, markerColor by night (mono: filled by day, hollow by night). The sun's elevation at each city is computed at run time from the clock. World regions only

dayColor.doc: A city's marker and halo while the sun is up there (daylight)

label.doc: Accessibility label (say what it shows: "World map, night over Asia"); a text object follows the data (a textMerge with a textFromFloat of the progress: "Flight 42 percent flown")

pitfalls: Geometry is fixed when the document is built (region, detail, borders, highlight, cities, states, the route's ends); at run time the app can colour countries (values + valueCountries), move points (pointsLon/pointsLat arrays), move the marker (markLon/markLat), advance the route (progress) and the clock moves the night

night assumes the world box ("world": latitudes 84 to -58, plate carrée): on a continent or a country it is not drawn correctly; leave it off there. The night side is one filled pathExpression along the terminator (atan(-cos(H) / tan(declination)))

Bytes grow with detail and borders: a world of land at low detail is ~6 KB, countries ~10 KB; Europe with borders at medium ~28 KB; each valueCountries entry adds its own outline (Europe's 48 at low ~30 KB). Prefer land for a backdrop and borders only where they matter

For anything else at map coordinates draw in your own canvas inside the same translate/scale: {"$mapPoint": {"region": ..., "lon": "@lon", "lat": "@lat"}} (x; "axis": "y" for y), {"$mapHeight": region} (the box height for width 1000), {"$mapRoute": {region, from, to, axis: "path" | "x" | "y" | "angle"}} (a great circle, or its samples as an array for arraySpline(@array, t)). In your own canvas use {"$map": {..., "outline": true}} for a stroked coast (a clipped fill's straight edges would show)
In mono the land is an outline (no fills), the highlight a fill, the night a grey shade
It fills the width it is given (fillMaxWidth): beside other content in a row, give it a weight or a width, or the row's other children get nothing

A list region frames those places, not a continent: ["Dubai", "London", "Singapore"]. Name the legs' cities in it (or [from, to] pairs, which add the arc's bulge): an arc to a place outside the frame leaves the map, routes are not clipped

legs draws each leg's arc and end dots; labels and the hub's name come from cities + labels (draw them too, the leg labels avoid them). With region, a label is placed for a map about 300 dp wide at the given height and a much smaller map can crowd them; with fit, text scales with the map and labels that would collide at a small size are hidden

fit + fill is the map that follows the window: {"fit": ["Dubai", "London"], "fill": true} takes the column's remaining height (put it last or give its siblings fixed sizes) and frames the places at whatever size the window has; the geometry covers boxes from 0.9:1 to 2.6:1 (outside that, blank bands)

ramp needs values + valueCountries; the values are raw (valueMin..valueMax, e.g. 0..250 €/MWh), not 0..1. Start the ramp with a colour unlike the land (not @colors.track), or the lowest values read as no data. Use borders: true so neighbours of close values stay apart, and legend: true for the scale

A world clock: night + twilight + sun + daylight with cities is the whole map of SHW-21: the soft edge (three shades), the sun over the subsolar point and city dots that glow where the sun is up. All three new options assume the world box (region "world" or "world-full") and repaint once a minute with the clock; the subsolar longitude ignores the equation of time (up to 4 degrees)
